explanation: Both captures are the same browser, the same width, and a page that has been settled: reduced motion, the page scrolled once, animations and transitions finished or stopped, fonts loaded, every image loaded and decoded, and two consecutive captures identical. The same drawing twice is the same picture, so the allowed difference is zero pixels. pixelmatch's per-pixel threshold is 0 and anti-aliased pixels are included (includeAA true), so every changed pixel counts. Image pixels are flattened to one colour on both sides before the diff, because the media pipeline re-encodes images; each image's box and aspect ratio are compared instead, and its similarity is reported. One differing pixel fails unless a register entry hides that element.
